advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where a per-child show_ticket fails once then succeeds on the second attempt, asserting the child's FULL state is kept, hierarchy_incomplete stays False, and show_ticket was called twice for that child (per-child retry teeth).
evidence: orchestrator.py:206-216 adds a separate per-child retry: `for attempt in range(_RETRY_ATTEMPTS): try: children.append(_reads.show_ticket(cid...)) ... except Exception: if attempt + 1 < _RETRY_ATTEMPTS: time.sleep(_RETRY_DELAY_S); continue`

test_partial_child_fetch_failure_records_child_id's `_show` raises for `_CHILD` on EVERY attempt (`if tid == _CHILD: raise RuntimeError("child unreadable")`) — exhaustion only, never fail-once-then-succeed.

test_retry_recovers_transient_enumeration_failure covers recovery ONLY for the enumeration loop (`calls["n"] == 1: raise ... return [...]`), with an explicit `assert calls["n"] == 2` teeth check; no equivalent exists for the per-child fetch.
ABSENCE: search of tests/unit/workflow for show_ticket monkeypatches finds no per-child fail-then-succeed case — a single-attempt per-child implementation would pass all tests.
advisory.finding: The per-child show_ticket retry loop has no recovery-path test: no test injects a transient per-child fetch failure that succeeds on the second attempt, so a regression reverting the per-child fetch to a single attempt (no retry) would still pass the entire suite. The enumeration loop has a dedicated recovery-teeth test (test_retry_recovers_transient_enumeration_failure), but the structurally-distinct per-child loop (orchestrator.py lines 206-216) is only tested for exhaustion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test_retry_recovers_transient_child_fetch: monkeypatch show_ticket so the child raises on its first call then returns full state on the second (tracked via a per-cid counter), then assert pctx.hierarchy_incomplete is False, the child's full state (not the summary) is in pctx.children, and the child was fetched exactly twice.
